content:
The image shows two ripe tomato fruits with significant fungal disease symptoms.

**Visual observations:**
- **Affected part**: Fruit (ripe tomatoes)
- **Left tomato**: Advanced lesion with dark black, sooty fungal growth — extensive necrosis with visible conidia/spore masses
- **Right tomato**: Classic circular, sunken, water-soaked lesion with a dark necrotic center and concentric ring pattern, pinkish-gray border
- Both lesions are depressed/sunken into the fruit surface, occurring on the blossom/lateral side
- The concentric ring arrangement of dark acervuli (spore-bearing structures) is prominent

**Reasoning through classes:**
- The **sunken, circular lesions with concentric dark rings** on ripe fruit are the hallmark of **Anthracnose** (*Colletotrichum* spp.)
- The dark spore masses (acervuli) arranged in concentric rings are characteristic
- Rhizopus soft rots tend to produce wispy black sporangiophores rather than structured concentric rings
- Alternaria black mold is more irregular and sooty without the defined concentric ring structure
- Gray mold would show fluffy gray mycelium
- The pattern on both fruits — especially the right one showing the classic early-to-mid-stage lesion — is textbook anthracnose on tomato
